Felipe, I cannot find you at your desk. Where are you?
I am at the warehouse. I am spending two days on site this week.
Two days? You normally go there for a morning.
Normally, yes. But the night shift is dealing with seven trucks a day instead of four.
That is a heavy workload. Is it permanent?
No, only this month. Two suppliers moved their dates. I am following up on that today.
And the report? The deadline is Friday, and the senior team meets at headquarters on Monday.
I know. I write it on Thursday nights, always. This week will be no different.
I usually work from the office, but this week I am on site.
At the moment we are dealing with a heavier workload.
The deadline is Friday, so I am following up on it today.
It is not permanent. It is only this month.
Give me one second. Let me put that in English.

Felipe, it is Megan with your week. The results meeting is still Monday at nine, at headquarters, and the report deadline has not moved. Tuesday is the problem. The audit team is arriving in the morning, so you are not going to the store after all. On Wednesday you are traveling to the warehouse, and you are staying there until Thursday afternoon, because the night shift wants twenty minutes with you. Friday is open for now. I am following up on the supplier contract today and I will send you the file tonight.

Morning, Felipe. Ian here, from the warehouse. Quick update before you arrive. We normally receive four trucks a day, but this week we are receiving seven, because two suppliers moved their dates. The night shift is dealing with the extra volume and nobody is complaining yet, although the workload is heavy. One machine is not working properly, so maintenance is coming on Thursday. Everything else is running as usual. See you on site on Wednesday.

First, Megan confirms that the results meeting is still on Monday at headquarters. Then she explains that the audit team is arriving on Tuesday morning. After that, she says the store visit is cancelled. Next, she describes the two days at the warehouse. Finally, she promises to follow up on the supplier contract.
